title: Rabbi Chizkiyah (of the Zohar)
author: Aharon Hyman

paragraphs: The one mentioned in the Zohar: see Noach 69b, where he went from Cappadocia to Lod and Rabbi Yesa met him; there, Vayetze 151a: “Rabbi Chiyya and Rabbi Chizkiyah were sitting,” etc.; there, Vayishlach 176b, he found Rabbi Yose, etc.; and there, 197b, he went with Rabbi Yesa from Cappadocia to Lod. There, Vayechi 226a, he learned from the chapters of Rav Yeiva Saba; there, 229b, he went on the road with Rabbi Yose and Rabbi Yehudah; there, 243b, he went with Rabbi Yose to see Rabbi Shimon in Cappadocia; there, Yitro 68b, he went with Rabbi Elazar and they saw a snake, and Rabbi Chizkiyah wanted to kill it, but Rabbi Elazar did not let him.

There, 86a, he went with Rabbi Yehudah from Cappadocia to Lod to see Rabbi Shimon. There, Pekudei 223b, he sat with Rabbi Abba and Rabbi Yose. There, Vayikra 4b, he asked Rabbi Shimon bar Yochai. There, 12b, he sat before Rabbi Yitzchak. There, Tazria 50b, he sat before Rabbi Shimon. There, Metzora 54a, he sat before Rabbi Elazar. There, Acharei 71a, he and Rabbi Yesa were in Gush Chalav.
In the Zohar, Naso 127b, he is called Rabbi Chizkiyah bar Rav.
And how fine is his homily in Naso 126a: “Your wife is like a fruitful vine — just as a vine accepts upon itself only its own [kind], so the wife of Israel … accepts upon herself only that mate.”

notes.text: Keep the accurate editorial qualifier of the Zohar: the Hebrew heading is only Rabbi Chizkiyah, but the first words explicitly set this entire notice in the Zohar. The reviewer’s removal is unnecessary. Yesa/Yose, Shimon, Elazar and bar Rav forms remain as supplied, without binding a historical identity.

The named Zohar Nasso node, consulted at text[4][15], directly names Chizkiyah in the vine homily. The supplied 126a pagination and the other listed folios were not independently aligned here. Failed folio-form requests are not evidence of absence; this notice remains specifically about the Zohar, without admitting a historical identity.
